1	# EHL Atira Challenge: priority plan
2	
3	Written 10 Oct 2026, 13:15 UTC, from every page of ehl-challenge.atira.ai, the run brief for `public-1`, the
4	starter kit and the API spec. Raw copies are in `notes/`.
5	
6	State of the board at that time: 25 teams, 4 ranked, best quality **21.5 / 100**, three teams at 0. The bar is low
7	right now. A bid that is signed, on the right tender, with the right materials and quantities, is already first.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. The game on one screen
12	
13	| | |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Job | One tender spread over 4 German websites: tender portal (Vergabeportal), supplier portal with the spec (Lieferantenportal), ERP, webmail (Werkpost). Apply the bid rules, enter one priced bid in the tender portal's configurator, sign it with a TAN from the mail. |
16	| Who decides | A model must choose where to go, what to search and which documents matter, at run time. Code may help: extract a page the model opened, parse a document it picked, paginate a result set it asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms. |
17	| Clock | Scored run 20 min. Test run up to 2 h (keep it under 20). Setup (max 5 min) and model warm-up are not counted. |
18	| Browsers | Up to 4 headful Chromium over CDP (`"browsers": 4` in agent.json). Starting your own browser gets it killed. |
19	| Models | Free hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (OpenAI API, tools, images, 256k) and Clef (yes/no, choice, score). Own keys allowed as team secrets, through the proxy, metered. |
20	| Answer | Entered on the website. Exactly one submission, and it ends the run. A run with no answer scores 0. |
21	| Ranking | Eligible (correct tender reference) → quality 0-100 → cost × time (lower is better). |
22	| Winners | 1. private dataset run, 2. public leaderboard, 3. elegance of the system. |
23	| Final run | Your **latest** submission that passed review (not your best), on a private dataset: other software, layout, site names, data, and the facts split differently across the sites. Same jobs, same rules, same answer format. |
24	
25	## 2. What this means (the rules that decide everything else)
26	
27	1. **Generalise, don't tune.** The final is on websites nobody has seen. No click paths, no URL paths, no CSS
28	   selectors tied to the public sites. The agent reads the brief at run time and finds things itself.
29	2. **Quality first, by far.** Cost × time only breaks ties at equal quality. Never trade points for speed. But the
30	   20 minutes are hard: a late answer is 0.
31	3. **The last upload is the one that goes to the final.** Never submit an experiment late in the day. Keep every
32	   tarball you submit, so you can re-submit a known good one.
33	4. **Opt in to best of 3** for the final (`atira final --best-of 3`). With the free models it costs nothing and only
34	   the best attempt counts.
35	5. **Eligibility is nearly free.** The tender reference is in the brief. The only way to lose it is to bid on a
36	   look-alike tender or not submit at all.
37	6. **The submission flow is the gate.** No signed bid means 0. Most teams are stuck there. Build it first.
38	
39	## 3. Where the 100 points are
40	
41	Bid case (from the brief and scoring docs):
42	
43	| Part | Points |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| Decision (bid / no_bid) | 5 |
46	| Tender reference | 5 |
47	| Discount percent | 5 |
48	| Total net, to the cent | 5 |
49	| Arithmetic consistency (total = sum of quantity × unit price) | 5 |
50	| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (when present) | 5 |
51	| Dated metal-index check (when present) | 5 |
52	| Positions, split evenly | 75 minus the two checks, so about 65 |
53	
54	Inside the positions block, summed over all positions (assuming the 65-point block):
55	
56	| Field | Weight | ≈ Points |
57	| --- | --- | --- |
58	| material_number | 20 % | 13 |
59	| quantity | 15 % | 9.75 |
60	| base_unit_price | 15 % | 9.75 |
61	| surcharge_per_unit | 10 % | 6.5 |
62	| packaging_per_unit | 10 % | 6.5 |
63	| rebate_total (project bonus) | 10 % | 6.5 |
64	| unit_price (final) | 10 % | 6.5 |
65	| lead_time_weeks | 10 % | 6.5 |
66	
67	No-bid case: decision 75, reference 5, no positions 5, total 0 → 15. A wrong bid / no_bid call is the most expensive
68	mistake in the game. Every field scores on its own, there is no penalty for a wrong value, so **always fill every
69	field with the best estimate rather than leave it blank.** Money is compared to the cent. Extra or duplicate
70	positions cost one position's share each.
71	
72	### The ladder (build in this order)
73	
74	| Step | What the agent gets right | Adds | Running total |
75	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
76	| A | Signed bid, right tender, decision, total = sum (code guarantees it) | 15 | 15 |
77	| B | Material per position + final quantity (incl. withdrawn Q&A, Satz → pieces) | ≈ 28 | ≈ 43 |
78	| C | Lead time (stock pooling, commitments) + discount (director mail, threshold) | ≈ 11.5 | ≈ 54 |
79	| D | Base price (valid condition, scale, price unit, FX to EUR) | ≈ 10 | ≈ 64 |
80	| E | Surcharge (metal index by date window, setup, shared setup pool) | ≈ 11.5 | ≈ 76 |
81	| F | Packaging + project bonus | ≈ 13 | ≈ 89 |
82	| G | Final unit price + total (only right when everything else is) | ≈ 11.5 | 100 |
83	
84	Step B alone beats today's leader. Steps A and B are where to spend the first half of the day.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 4. Priorities, in order
89	
90	### P0. Setup (first 30 min)
91	
92	- [ ] Ask the organizers now: submission deadline, when the final run starts, prizes. Read `/announcements`.
93	- [ ] Team on the site (up to 5, GitHub invites). `atira login` on each laptop.
94	- [ ] `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` so Claude Code can start test runs, read logs and see screenshots.
95	- [ ] `atira final --best-of 3` (can be changed until the final starts, do it now so it is never forgotten).
96	- [ ] GitHub repo created and linked on the team page (organizers ask for it, and elegance is judged on code).
97	- [ ] Starter kit in `ehl-hackathon/agent/`. **That folder is the package root.** Notes and hand-solved answers stay
98	      outside it and out of git.
99	- [ ] `atira models proxy` running in its own terminal; `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` in the dev terminal.
100	
101	### P1. Hand-solve public-1 once (60-90 min, in parallel with P2 if you have teammates)
102	
103	- Log into the 4 sites with the scouting logins (`atira scout`) and work out the whole answer by hand, rule by rule.
104	  Save it as `notes/expected-public-1.json`. Never copy it into `agent/`.
105	- Why: test runs show points per field but never the right values. A hand answer lets you diff every field in
106	  seconds on local runs, and it forces you to understand every rule before coding it.
107	- While doing it, write down **patterns, not values**: where each kind of fact lives, how search works, what breaks
108	  (popups, timeouts, paging, iframes, ZIPs). These become generic hints in the prompt.
109	
110	### P2. Thin end-to-end that submits (the gate)
111	
112	- Generic browser tools (section 5). Login, cookie wall, error retry and re-login are helpers.
113	- Submitter agent that takes a finished answer JSON plus the brief's submission paragraph and completes the form,
114	  the TAN and the final dialog. Test it locally with a dummy answer (scouting submissions never count).
115	- First goal: Step A + B. Then **submit once** to get on the board with an eligible result.
116	
117	### P3. Climb the ladder (C → G)
118	
119	- Each step is: a fact the investigators must find + a function in the calculator + a unit test.
120	- After each step: local run → diff against `expected-public-1.json` → test run in the sandbox for the breakdown.
121	- Submit a new scored version whenever test runs show a clear gain and it is stable over 2+ runs.
122	
123	### P4. Robustness for the private dataset (this is what wins)
124	
125	- Grep the package for any public value: tender reference, company name, VAT id, material numbers, prices, names,
126	  URL paths, German button labels not in the brief. Zero hits.
127	- Never assume which site holds which fact. The investigators collect every fact type they see, and a gap check
128	  sends targeted searches to any site for what is still missing.
129	- Every UI wording the submitter uses comes from the brief at run time, not from code.
130	- Run 3-4 test runs of the same package in parallel. Judge by the worst run, not the best.
131	- Handle no_bid end to end (Verzichtserklärung path) even though public-1 is probably a bid.
132	
133	### P5. Speed and cost (only once quality is flat)
134	
135	- Small observations, prompt caching (cached Qwen input is about 10× cheaper), 4 browsers in parallel.
136	- Clef for cheap yes/no calls (is this the current revision, is this the right mail).
137	- Only the tie-break uses this, plus a possible small prize for the fastest, cheapest passing run.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 5. Architecture to build
142	
143	**Model decides, code checks, code computes.** That is robust, easy to defend in review, and reads as elegant.
144	
145	```
146	brief (run time) ──► planner: list of facts the rules need
147	                         │
148	     ┌──────────────┬────┴─────────┬──────────────┐
149	     ▼              ▼              ▼              ▼
150	 tender agent   spec agent     mail agent     erp agent        (one browser each, LLM-driven loops)
151	 (browser 1)    (browser 2)    (browser 3)    (browser 4)
152	     └──────────────┴──── evidence ledger ────────┘            (every fact: value, source URL, date, sender, quote)
153	                         │
154	                   gap check (model) ──► targeted follow-up searches
155	                         │
156	                   rules engine (pure Python, Decimal) ──► answer JSON + self-checks
157	                         │
158	                   submitter agent (tender portal + TAN from mail) ──► signed bid
159	```
160	
161	### Browser tools (generic, the same on any website)
162	
163	- `observe()`: compact page text plus numbered interactive elements, tables as rows, content of iframes included.
164	  Keep it small. Screenshot only when the text is ambiguous (Qwen reads images).
165	- `click(ref)`, `type(ref, text)`, `select(ref, option)`, `press(key)`, `goto(url)`, `open_tab()`.
166	- `download_and_read(ref)`: fetch a file the model chose, unzip, extract PDF/HTML/CSV text.
167	- Auto-helpers the model never has to think about: cookie wall, flaky error page retry, session expired → log in
168	  again with the run's credentials and return, JS dialogs logged and accepted.
169	- Never use the browser Back button in the bid form (it clears later steps).
170	
171	### Agents
172	
173	- Investigators: one loop per site, with a `record_fact` tool. Each fact carries type, key, value, unit, date with
174	  timezone, sender, tender reference and a short quote. The model chooses searches and pages.
175	- ERP agent starts per position once the requirement (after amendments and stroke derivation) and Kataloggruppe are
176	  known. Positions can be looked up in parallel tabs.
177	- The model makes the important choices (which tender, which revision is current, which material matches, which mail
178	  applies). Code then checks them against the rules (dates, exact reference, sender domain, exact attribute match). If
179	  code disagrees, show the model the conflict and let it decide again.
180	
181	### Rules engine (pure function, the core of the score)
182	
183	- `Decimal` everywhere, `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Python `round()` is banker's rounding and will lose cents.
184	- One function per brief rule, with the rule quoted in a comment, and unit tests with obviously fake numbers.
185	- Output is always schema-valid, and `total_net` always equals the sum of quantity × unit price.
186	
187	### Clock guard
188	
189	- Read `expires_at` from the run. Target: investigation done by about minute 10, submission started by minute 13 at
190	  the latest, whatever is missing.
191	- Below about 5 minutes left: stop everything, compute with what you have, submit. A partial bid with the right
192	  reference beats a perfect bid that is late.
193	- Measure how long the submission flow takes in test runs and set the cut-off from that number.
194	
195	### Models
196	
197	- Start with Qwen for everything: free, unlimited test runs, tiny simulated cost.
198	- If one step keeps failing (multi-step rule reading, long mails), move only that step to a stronger model with your
199	  own key as a team secret. Quality beats cost.
200	- Retry model calls on 5xx and timeouts. A cold model can take minutes, so use long timeouts.
201	- Hosted limits: 32 Qwen calls and 16 Clef calls in flight per team, across all runs.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 6. Rule traps checklist
206	
207	Each line is a place where points leak. Tick it when the agent handles it and a test covers it.
208	
209	**Tender and Q&A**
210	- [ ] Right tender: exact reference from the brief, look-alike tenders exist.
211	- [ ] Documents behind "expression of interest" (Teilnahme bekunden): do it early.
212	- [ ] Iframes, ZIP files, flaky error pages, cookie wall.
213	- [ ] Quantity = latest dated Q&A change for that position; withdrawn answers (zurückziehen) are ignored, then the
214	      latest remaining change applies, else the tender quantity.
215	- [ ] Units: Satz × pieces per set from the **governing** spec revision. Every bid quantity is in pieces.
216	- [ ] Q&A also assigns: Konditionsgruppe, packaging tariff key, delivery commitment key, shared setup pool members,
217	      technical amendments. Collect all of them.
218	
219	**Specification**
220	- [ ] The portal opens the oldest revision first. Use the one marked current.
221	- [ ] Nested document viewers and paged requirement tables (read every page).
222	- [ ] Scoped amendments: only those naming that revision and requirement, only the named attributes, latest dated per
223	      attribute wins.
224	- [ ] "nutzbarer Weg": nominal stroke = amended usable stroke + 2 × per-end reserve from the revision-specific
225	      Technikfreigabe mail.
226	- [ ] Kataloggruppe per requirement is the ERP search key.
227	
228	**ERP**
229	- [ ] SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, short session timeout (auto re-login).
230	- [ ] Search by Kataloggruppe, narrow to 20 or fewer results (empty or broad searches show nothing).
231	- [ ] Exact match on bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification. Normalise units before comparing.
232	- [ ] Active only. Blocked materials do not qualify. No match for any position → no_bid. Re-check before declaring
233	      it (a missed stroke derivation looks exactly like "no match").
234	- [ ] Price condition valid on the scenario date, both endpoints inclusive.
235	- [ ] Scale with the highest minimum quantity ≤ final quantity, per position (not per material sum).
236	- [ ] Price unit (for example per 100 pieces) normalised to per piece.
237	- [ ] Currency + FX key → Devisenfixing mail → EUR, HALF_UP to cents. That rounded EUR base is used everywhere after.
238	- [ ] Stock, stock lead time, production lead time, pieces per carton, allocation mass, surcharge mass, ordinary setup.
239	
240	**Mail**
241	- [ ] Search is AND: tender reference + topic word. Read inbox **and** archive, all pages.
242	- [ ] Authorised sender = right local part **and** the bidder's own mailbox domain. Look-alike domains do not count.
243	- [ ] Latest record dated no later than the scenario date, exact reference. Future-dated and other references never
244	      apply. A newer record replaces an older one, even if its condition fails.
245	- [ ] Discount (leitung@): latest exact-reference approval. If it has a minimum order value: undiscounted net value
246	      (base × quantity, no surcharge, no setup, rounded) ≥ threshold, inclusive. If it fails, 0 %, no fallback.
247	- [ ] Konditionsregeln (kalkulation@): group → discount on base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup never
248	      discounted. No group → base only.
249	- [ ] Preisindizes (kalkulation@): rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last one listed.
250	- [ ] Technikfreigabe (technik@), Verpackungstarife and Terminfreigabe (logistik@), Devisenfixing and Projektbonus
251	      (finanzen@), Rüstpools (kalkulation@).
252	- [ ] TAN: request it only right before signing, use the newest TAN mail, valid 5 min, a new request kills the old.
253	
254	**Calculation**
255	- [ ] Shared stock: sum final quantities per material. Stock must cover the whole sum, else every position of that
256	      material uses production lead time.
257	- [ ] Delivery commitment: only if its material matches and pooled demand for that material ≤ ceiling (inclusive),
258	      else the shared-stock rule.
259	- [ ] Packaging: ceil(pieces / carton size) × tariff, per position, divided by pieces. Never changes quantity. Never
260	      discounted.
261	- [ ] Shared setup: one pool fee split by quantity × allocation mass with the cent rule given in the Rüstpools mail,
262	      added to each member's ordinary setup.
263	- [ ] surcharge_per_unit = mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + shared setup) / pieces, before discount.
264	- [ ] Project bonus: marginal bands (like tax brackets) on the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, round once,
265	      split by largest remainder in cents, ties by ascending position id. rebate_total is per position, not per piece.
266	      0.00 for non-members.
267	- [ ] Final unit price = discounted base + discounted mass surcharge + (setup + shared setup + cartons − bonus) /
268	      pieces, from unrounded parts, rounded HALF_UP once.
269	- [ ] total_net = Σ quantity × rounded unit price, rounded HALF_UP.
270	- [ ] Timezones: tender portal shows Europe/Athens, ERP shows UTC, the scenario date is UTC. Convert all to UTC.
271	- [ ] German numbers: "1.234,56" is 1234.56, and "1.234" is one thousand two hundred thirty-four. Enter prices in
272	      German format in the form.
273	
274	## 7. Submission flow (public-1 wording, from the brief)
275	
276	The private brief will name its own steps, so the submitter follows the brief, not these words.
277	
278	1. Teilnahme bekunden for the exact tender (also unlocks documents, so do it during investigation).
279	2. Angebotsabgabe → register the bidder with the company name and USt-IdNr given in the brief.
280	3. Hauptangebot for bid, Verzichtserklärung for no_bid.
281	4. Configurator: per position material, quantity, prices, lead time, breakdown fields. "Position auslassen" only for
282	   positions you really have nothing for.
283	5. Net unit prices and net total in German format. The gross figure shown includes VAT, ignore it.
284	6. Acknowledge the tender documents.
285	7. Request TAN → read the newest TAN in the webmail → enter it within 5 minutes.
286	8. Read the summary page and compare it with the computed answer before confirming.
287	9. Confirm "Angebot verbindlich abgeben" in the browser dialog (Playwright: handle `page.on("dialog")`).
288	
289	Session expiry loses unsaved entries, so compute everything first and fill the form in one go. Going back clears
290	later steps.
291	
292	## 8. Fair-play red lines (a reject means no run at all)
293	
294	- Any value from the public scenario in code, prompts, notes, tests or defaults: tender reference, company, VAT id,
295	  material numbers, prices, discounts, totals, logins, TANs. Read them from the brief and the sites at run time.
296	- A fixed click path, a crawler that dumps the sites into one model call, or a model used only as a fallback.
297	- Calling any host other than the platform and the 4 sites, any model outside the proxy, a local model, or your own
298	  browser.
299	- API keys in the package (use team secrets).
300	- Text that tries to steer the AI reviewer counts against you. A plain README explaining the design is fine.
301	- Test fixtures must use clearly fake numbers so the reviewer never mistakes them for copied values.
302	
303	## 9. Iteration loop
304	
305	```sh
306	atira models proxy                         # terminal 1, keep open
307	eval "$(atira scout --env)"                # terminal 2
308	uv run --no-sync python agent.py           # local run against the public sites (nothing counts)
309	python ../notes/diff.py out.json           # your own diff against the hand answer (keep outside agent/)
310	atira test-run . --follow                  # sandbox run with the per-field score breakdown
311	atira submit .                             # review, then one scored run on the public board
312	atira status
313	```
314	
315	- Up to 4 test runs at a time per team, 3 more can wait. Use them in parallel to measure variance.
316	- In Claude Code with the MCP: `diagnose_run`, `run_screenshot`, `run_profile`, `compare_runs`.
317	- One scored submission in flight at a time. Review takes minutes, the run up to 20. Plan about 30-40 min per cycle.
318	
319	## 10. Final-hour protocol
320	
321	- [ ] Feature freeze about 90 min before the deadline.
322	- [ ] 3-4 parallel test runs of the candidate. Pick the package with the best **worst** run.
323	- [ ] Submit it no later than 60 min before the deadline. Wait for review passed and the score.
324	- [ ] If it regresses, re-submit the last good tarball (`atira package <sub_id> --out dir`) so that one is latest.
325	- [ ] `atira status` shows best of 3. Repo linked. Nothing submitted after the final candidate.
326	
327	## 11. Demo day (if picked)
328	
329	- One-line start: `atira test-run ./agent` opens the live run view (timer, model calls, cost, score).
330	- Download a recording of a good run as fallback (`GET /v1/runs/<id>/video`).
331	- The pitch in three lines: the model navigates and decides, code checks and computes, every number in the bid points
332	  to its source in the evidence ledger.
333	
334	## 12. Still unknown
335	
336	- Submission deadline and final run time: ask the organizers.
337	- How many private scenarios, and whether one could be a no_bid case: build for both.
338	- The logged-in side of the 4 sites was not scouted for this plan. Confirm the traps in section 6 during the

1	# Prepare a tender response
2	
3	You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.
4	
5	Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.
6	
7	## Rules
8	
9	1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
10	2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
11	3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
12	4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
13	5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
14	6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
15	7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
16	8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.
17	
18

=================== README.md
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)

"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]

"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's

async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
    """TODO: your agent goes here.

    `task` is the run: task["brief"] (the task and its rules), task["access"] (each website's url and login),
    task["submission"] (where the answer goes) and task["answer_schema"]. `page` is a Playwright page in browser 1.

    For an "api" submission, return the answer and main() submits it. For a "site" submission, enter the answer on
    that website yourself, then return None.

    Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `contract.seconds_left(task)` says how many are left. Every part
    of the answer scores on its own, so stop and submit your best answer about a minute before the end; an answer
    that comes too late scores 0.
    """
    return None


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        answer = await solve(task, page)
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1

class FakeServer:
    """One HTTP server for the API and the models: answers each request with the next scripted reply per path."""

    def __init__(self, replies: dict[str, list[tuple[int, dict]]]):
        self.replies, self.requests = replies, []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def handle_one(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)) if length else None
                # self.headers matches header names in any case: urllib sends X-api-key
                fake.requests.append({"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": self.headers,
                                      "body": body})
                status, reply = fake.replies[self.path].pop(0)
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = handle_one

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

- Each scored run has 20 minutes and allows one submission. No answer scores 0.
- A model must decide where to go and what to search. Fixed click paths, crawlers, or a model used only as a fallback get rejected.
- **Winners are picked mostly on a final run on private websites nobody has seen** (other software, layouts and data). The public leaderboard comes second, then how well the system is designed.

Exit code 1
## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```sh
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
  "questions": {"next": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "What next?",
    "criteria": {
      "retry": "Retry the request",
      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```sh
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
| Team | Up to 5 people. |

## The task

One tender, four German websites, one bid.

The agent produces: **One bid**. It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.

## The websites

Each run gets its own logins, in the run's `access`. To look around yourself, use the scouting logins below. Expect what real business software throws at you: popups, session timeouts, outdated documents and look-alike records. Everything your agent needs fits on a 1280×800 screen.

### 1. Tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`

- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run>

## Public and private data

There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

## Bid rules
-----
## How a run works

Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).

1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.

### Develop locally

```sh
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
```

`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.

Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:

curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
```

The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. | `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |

| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |

A submission is your agent as a gzipped tarball. It is reviewed automatically, then run once in the sandbox on the public dataset, and that score ranks your team. Every submission is measured on its run in the sandbox.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.

- **Time:** Wall-clock time from the start of the run until the answer is accepted. It weighs as much as cost: halving either halves cost × time.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:

| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

-----
## Scored run

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:

- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
  and the websites.
- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.

1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
   right after setup:

   ```json
   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
   ```

   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.

   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
   run that answered keeps its result.
3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |

The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
ends without an answer scores 0.

## Browsers

The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:

```json
{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
```

`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
| `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |

**At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
`[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
recording of each afterwards.

On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
browsers.

# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.

Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

## Flagged results

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
